evidence.text: Q3 GAAP results should include a one-off credit of about $23.5m from the Sonate/Vegadelphia trademark case. The 10-Q balance sheet carried $38.9m of accrued litigation expense at both 2025-12-31 and 2026-06-27, the full jury verdict of $23.5m plus $15.4m. On 2026-09-18 the court cut actual damages to $37,500 and entered judgment for $15,437,500. That points to roughly a $23.5m reversal inside a quarter whose GAAP operating loss has run about $30m (Q2: -$30.8m, which itself included an $11.0m arbitration credit). The headline GAAP loss could therefore be far smaller than run-rate. Adjusted EBITDA is likely unaffected, and the $15.4m judgment is still a cash outflow unless appealed or bonded.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q2 2026 GAAP net income was +$16.4m (from a $57.7m debt-extinguishment gain and the $11m arbitration credit) and the stock still fell 13.4%. evidence.why_not_priced: The ruling is public in an 8-K, but EPS consensus on a three-analyst name may not have been reset for the reversal. Any headline GAAP 'beat' would come from this one-off, and the market has looked through such items twice this year. If it were unpriced as positive information, the stock would have moved on 2026-09-22. It did not move visibly.
evidence.independence: The accrual figure comes from the Q2 10-Q balance sheet (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1655210/000165521026000055/bynd-20260627.htm). Two company documents, one fact.

evidence.text: Financing overhang. The company can no longer use Form S-3 or its ATM (Q2 release). evidence.text: The bar sits inside management's own Q3 framing. Consensus revenue of about $800M (+10% on Q3 2025's $725.1M) matches what follows from three numbers: CELSIUS brand Q2 2026 net sales of $387.0M (-11.7%), management's statement that Q3 brand sales will look 'a lot like Q2', and Jefferies' projection of CELSIUS brand sales down 12%. Q3 2025 brand sales were about $382.6M, so -12% gives about $337M. Add Rockstar at about $66M (Q2 run-rate) and the consensus needs Alani Nu at about $392M, +18% on Q3 2025's $332.0M. Alani tracked scans are running about +50%. B. Riley models $817.6M, about 2% above consensus, even after assuming about $35M of further inventory rebalancing.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 revenue missed by about 6% ($818M vs $870M) and the stock fell 18.46%. Q3 2025 beat on revenue ($725.1M vs $715.7M) and EPS (42c vs 28c), yet the stock fell 24.8% on Q4 'noise' commentary. Q4 2025 and Q1 2026 beats were bought (+6.9%, +4.5%). The reported-quarter line pays only when the forward commentary does not override it.
evidence.why_not_priced: Consensus has already been cut (the revenue estimate fell 7.6% over three months per Chartmill, and targets were cut at JPM, UBS, TD Cowen and Jefferies). The gap between Alani's roughly 50% scan growth and the roughly 18% the bar needs is the part not in the consensus. Had the market priced a clear Alani-led beat, consensus would have moved back up toward the B. Riley number; it has not. Partly priced: the 5-day run-up of +11.8% suggests some of the street is already leaning toward a beat.
evidence.independence: Brand decline rate and Q3 framing: the 8-K Q2 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001341766/000134176626000047/ex9912q2026.htm) and the call summary (https://www.chartmill.com/news/external/114221/celh-q2-earnings-call-flags-core-brand-reset-before-2027). Q3 2025 base: the 8-K Q3 2025 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1341766/000134176625000138/ex9913q2025.htm). The arithmetic is mine. The Jefferies figure and the B. Riley model come from the same Investing.com article.

evidence.text: The Goldman Sachs Q3 2026 c-store retailer survey shows the CELSIUS brand -1% year on year against an energy category +11% (+10% in Q2) and Alani Nu +47%. That is a stable CELSIUS brand, close to Q2's -2% tracked retail, not a further deterioration, plus strong Alani sell-through. Separately, IRI scans quoted around the 2026-09-08 Barclays conference showed CELSIUS -5% to -10% and Alani about +50%.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q2 2026 tracked retail was -2% but net sales were -11.7%, and the stock fell 18.5%. Scan-to-shipment gaps, not scans themselves, have driven the misses, so a sell-through proxy transmits only partly.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is a channel survey published 2026-10-23 that wire previews do not quote, and it covers one channel. If it were fully priced, CELSIUS-brand estimates would not still sit at about -12%. The survey fits that number, since shipments trail sell-through while distributor inventory is rebalanced. So this is mostly confirmation that Alani is strong; it is not evidence of a brand beat.
evidence.independence: Proxy, not company data. The IRI scan ranges are reported in the B. Riley/Investing.com note (https://www.investing.com/news/analyst-ratings/briley-reiterates-buy-on-celsius-stock-ahead-of-q3-results-93CH-4990506) and in the TIKR Barclays recap (https://www.tikr.com/es/blog/celsius-stock-slid-nearly-7-after-barclays-and-the-real-payoff-it-described-waits-until-2027). KDP's Q3 also says the energy category kept growing: Ghost passed $1B retail and KDP energy share passed 10%.

evidence.text: The forward line is the risk, and management has already deferred the payoff. On the Q2 call it said the CELSIUS brand improves only gradually from Q4 and returns to growth in 2027, and that the Q4 Alani Nu comparison is distorted by the prior-year inventory build for the PepsiCo transition. At Barclays (2026-09-08) the CFO said the real dollars from revenue management are 'a game for '27 and '28', not a rescue for H2 2026. There is room for Q4 commentary that resets Alani Q4 below the street.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 beat on revenue and EPS but fell 24.8% when the CFO warned of Q4 'noise' from the Alani/Pepsi rollout. Forward commentary has decided at least two of the last seven reactions.
evidence.why_not_priced: The deferral itself is public, which is why the stock fell after Barclays and targets were cut. What is not priced is the size of the Q4 Alani comparison headwind, which the company has never quantified. A run-up of +11.8% in five days into the print suggests some holders are positioned for an H2 inflection that management has said is a 2027 event.
evidence.independence: Same deferral reported from the Barclays session: https://www.tikr.com/es/blog/celsius-stock-slid-nearly-7-after-barclays-and-the-real-payoff-it-described-waits-until-2027. evidence.text: Can costs peaked inside Q3 cost of goods. The US Midwest aluminum premium hit a record of about $1.19/lb in June 2026 and eased only to about $1.09-1.10 by mid-September. Can pricing passes through with a lag of two to three months, so Q3 gross margin carries the peak. Management guided gross margin to the high 40s (Q2: 48.1%).
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 gross margin was 48.1% (-340bp year on year) and the EBITDA miss contributed to the -18.5% move.
evidence.why_not_priced: Largely priced. It sits inside the company's high-40s guide, and consensus EPS of $0.34 is below Q2's $0.36. Only an outcome below 47% would be new.
evidence.independence: Mysteel on the pass-through lag: https://www.mysteel.net/news/5103982-us-aluminum-midwest-premiums-hit-record-high-what-drives-the-surge-and-who-bears-the-cost. It is a proxy.

evidence.why_not_priced: The stake itself is priced. No 13D, proxy filing or settlement has appeared on EDGAR since (the last filings are Form 4s and a 13G/A on 08-14), so any call-day governance news would be new. Its probability is unknown, so it is sized small.

evidence.text: On 2026-09-08, with about three weeks of the quarter left, Chime raised Q3 guidance to about $705m revenue (~30% YoY) and $117-120m adjusted EBITDA, from $680-690m and $105-110m. Consensus moved onto it: $705.2m revenue and $0.09 EPS, with a $0.15 whisper. In Q2 the company beat the top of its guide by about 4% ($670m against $633-643m), but that guide was set a full quarter ahead. A guide set with three weeks left leaves much less room, so the revenue beat is likely around 1% and the whisper sets a high bar for EPS.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (5 Aug): beat the top of guide by about 4% and raised FY, +20.56%. Q1 2026 (6 May): EPS $0.13 against $0.03 consensus and a FY raise, but the stock fell 12.52% on a cautious outlook and Chime Prime margin worries. Q3 2025: -5.39% despite a raise. The stock trades on the outlook, not on the size of the beat.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: consensus sits on the guide and the stock rose 5.9% on the raise day. What is not visible is how small the revenue beat can be once the bar was reset mid-quarter. If the market fully saw that, the whisper would sit nearer consensus and the stock would not have run up 8% in the 20 days before the print.
evidence.independence: Consensus and whisper are from Earnings Whispers via Finviz, 2026-10-27 (https://finviz.com/news/409422/chimes-stride-bank-deal-lifts-the-bar-as-prime-and-instant-loans-face-a-proof-quarter). The Q2 beat history is from the Q2 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001795586/000179558626000046/ex991q226.htm) and the Q1 release's Q2 guide of $633-643m (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001795586/000179558626000035/ex991q126.htm).

evidence.text: Q3 carries $16-20m of net cash restructuring charges from the ~10% workforce cut announced 2026-07-31. A $9-12m reversal of stock compensation partly offsets it, for a net income hit of $6-9m (about $0.02 a share on ~380m shares). This makes the GAAP EPS bar ($0.06-0.09) noisy. Adjusted EBITDA likely excludes the charges.
evidence.source_date: 2026-08 (10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-06-30, subsequent-events note)
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior restructuring quarter on this name. The stock barely moved when the cut was announced (secondary summaries).
evidence.why_not_priced: It is disclosed, so it is largely priced. The risk is a headline GAAP EPS miss against an aggregator EPS that did not net out the charge. If that were fully understood, the two EPS consensus sources would not disagree ($0.06 vs $0.09).
evidence.independence: The 8-K of 2026-07-31 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001795586/000179558626000046/chym-20260731.htm) is the same disclosure, so the two count as one source.

evidence.text: Management raised MyPay limits to $1,000 and said loss rates would rise modestly. MyPay's Q2 loss rate was 0.9% and its transaction profit $73m, so a rise in losses could take a little off transaction margin (73% in Q2) in Q3/Q4.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Unknown for this line on its own. Q1 2026's -12.5% was tied to margin worries about Chime Prime, so margin quality has moved this stock.
evidence.why_not_priced: The company guided to it, so it sits inside what the market was told and is sized near zero. It only matters if the rise is larger than 'modest'. If the market feared that, the EBITDA guide raise to $117-120m would have been discounted, and it was not.
evidence.independence: The Q2 release gives the 0.9% loss rate and $73m transaction profit (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001795586/000179558626000046/ex991q226.htm). No independent read on Q3 losses.

evidence.text: The Bancorp (TBBK) is one of Chime's two partner banks. It reported Q3 2026 card gross dollar volume of $54.3bn, +23.4% YoY and +1.6% QoQ. Chime's own Q2 purchase volume grew 17% (20% including OIT), so partner-bank volume held up through the quarter. It is a proxy: Bancorp's GDV includes many other fintech programmes.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Purchase volume and payments revenue are 64% of revenue ($430m of $670m in Q2). Q2's volume and revenue beat came with +20.6%.
evidence.why_not_priced: A counterparty print after Chime last spoke (8 Sep), but the ~30% revenue guide already implies strong volume. If the market had read it as upside, revenue consensus would sit above the $705m point guide rather than on it.
evidence.independence: Proxy only. Visa's fiscal Q4 release shows total payments volume +9% (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001403161/000140316126000126/q42026earningsrelease.htm), but I could not extract the US debit figure.

That supports the read of a healthy consumer-fintech acquisition environment going into Chime's Q3, a seasonally strong quarter for member adds against its 1.8M FY net-add target (about 900k needed in H2).
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Member adds have mattered: Q1 2026 added ~700k (beat), but the stock fell on the outlook. The 1.8M target, raised from 1.4M in Q2, came with +20.6%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Peer read-through is transmission, not Chime's own number. Some of it is in the 20-day run-up of +8%. If fully priced, the put skew would not be +10.65.

evidence.text: The Department of War Office of Strategic Capital issued a conditional commitment (2026-10-07) for up to $1.5B of 30-year senior secured delayed-draw financing. Definitive agreements, approvals, appropriations and consents under existing debt are still outstanding, and warrants of up to 7.5% of fully diluted equity would be issued as tranches fund. The CFO had called refinancing the roughly $630M of ~16% first-lien debt the top priority (08-19 call). The call may give a definitive-agreement or refinancing update.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The announcement drew +27% after hours on 10-07, then the stock round-tripped to below the pre-news level by 11-04.
evidence.why_not_priced: The full round-trip of the +27% spike shows the market now assigns little probability to funding. A dated path to definitive agreements, or a cheaper refinancing of the 16% first-lien, would re-price it. On the financing question, the money buys long-dated capacity capital at government cost against 16% debt, with $1.09B of cash on hand, so this is not distress money. It is a positive or zero, minus the 7.5% warrant dilution.
evidence.independence: 08-19 call: about $630M of first-lien at about 16% is the top refinancing priority, gross-margin breakeven at about $800M annual revenue run rate, https://www.tradingkey.com/news/transcripts/262119459-tradingkey. A separate document.
